target_moa.text: Elotuzumab is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody that binds SLAMF7 on myeloma cells and NK cells, directly activating NK cells and recruiting circulating NK cells to the vicinity of the myeloma cell.

citations.quote: On June 29, 2015 Bristol-Myers-Squibb submitted a Biologic License Application (BLA) for elotuzumab, a humanized immunoglobulin G1 (IgG1) monoclonal antibody (mAb) targeted against Signaling Lymphocyte Activation Molecule Family 7 (SLAMF7).
Binding of elotuzumab to SLAMF7 on NK cells in vitro caused upregulation of CD69, increased cytokine production, and degranulation, implicating direct NK cell activation as a mechanism of action.

EMPLICITI® (elotuzumab) is a humanized recombinant monoclonal immunoglobulin G1 (IgG1) that binds human Signaling Lymphocyte Activation Molecule F7 (SLAMF7) on the surface of myeloma cells and recruits circulating Natural Killer (NK) cells to the vicinity of the myeloma cell.

EMPLICITI is a SLAMF7-directed immunostimulatory antibody indicated in combination with lenalidomide and dexamethasone for the treatment of patients with multiple myeloma who have received one to three prior therapies. (1)

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>=20%): fatigue, diarrhea, pyrexia, constipation, cough, peripheral neuropathy, nasopharyngitis, upper respiratory tract infection, decreased appetite, pneumonia. Warnings include infusion reactions (~10% of patients), infections, second primary malignancies (9.1% E-Ld vs 5.7% Ld), and hepatotoxicity. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 65.4% (EMPLICITI) vs 56.5% (control).

citations.quote: Most common adverse reactions (20% or higher) are fatigue, diarrhea, pyrexia, constipation, cough, peripheral neuropathy, nasopharyngitis, upper respiratory tract infection, decreased appetite, pneumonia. (6.1)

EMPLICITI can cause infusion reactions. Infusion reactions were reported in approximately 10% of patients treated with EMPLICITI with lenalidomide and dexamethasone in the randomized trial in multiple myeloma.

In a clinical trial of patients with multiple myeloma (N=635), invasive second primary malignancies (SPM) have been observed in 9.1% of patients treated with E-Ld and 5.7% of patients treated with Ld.
Serious adverse reactions were reported in 65.4% of patients treated on the EMPLICITI arm and 56.5% for patients treated on the control arm.
